item.p: Collations: the Unicode codepoint collation and the HTML ASCII case-insensitive collation (both required by F&O 4.0), and UCA collation URIs with fallback (on by default): codepoint order, with strength primary and secondary matching case-blind (QT4 simple-uca-fallback). Full UCA (DUCET tables, tailoring, numeric and case-order options; advanced-uca-fallback) stays out: the tables cost more wasm size than the 81 tests that need them are worth. fallback=no on a UCA URI is FOCH0002.

Out: fn:parse-html and fn:html-doc (an HTML5 tree builder is its own project; 1,400 QT4 cases, excluded by ), invisible XML, schema awareness (validate is XQST0075; XSLT validation="strict" and type attributes raise XTSE1660, as for a basic processor), streaming (streamable="yes" runs unstreamed, as a non-streaming processor may), the Update Facility (its tests are not run; %updating is rejected statically), Full Text, EXPath, XPath 1.0 compatibility mode and XSLT backwards-compatible behaviour, civil-timezone and Olson names (no tz database), calendars other than AD and ISO and languages other than English in format-date and format-integer (the fallback markers F&O allows).
Later in this plan: fn:serialize with every method (3.4), fn:load-xquery-module (3.11); fn:transform only if Phase 4 sweeps leave time.

Hand-written scanners: regex syntax (), picture strings of the formatting functions and CSV are scanned by hand, because their lexical rules are run-time options (decimal formats, CSV delimiters) that a tree-sitter grammar cannot take. Everything else keeps , including XSLT value templates (grammars/value_template).
